subtopic: Dead code elimination on ops with side effects
learningObjective: Explain why dead code elimination (DCE) in a tensor IR must respect ops that have side effects, and how the IR encodes this.
stem: A tensor-IR pass tries to run DCE and removes both `linalg.copy` (writes to %B) and `linalg.matmul` (returns a used %C) below. Which statement most accurately describes what DCE is allowed to remove in this snippet?

options.text: DCE may remove `linalg.copy` (its result appears unused inside the function) and the pure `arith.addf` (unused); `linalg.matmul` must stay because its result escapes.

DCE may remove only the pure `arith.addf` because it has no observable side effects and its result is dead. Neither `linalg.copy` nor `linalg.matmul` can be removed: both have write side effects, and the copy's write to %B is externally observable through the function's memref argument.

DCE may remove all three operations because pass-by-memref semantics let the caller re-execute the code path; the callee is free to elide any write it does not itself observe internally. In this reading, pass-by-memref is equivalent to pure-value semantics because the compiler owns the buffer and only surfaces the writes through an explicit return value; thus stores to it are private to the callee.

DCE may remove `linalg.copy` and `linalg.matmul` but must keep `arith.addf` because SSA values are always considered live regardless of use, whereas memref stores are always dead absent an explicit `sync` op. Under this framing, MLIR's default DCE ignores memory-effect annotations entirely and treats any op whose SSA result is unused as removable, on the assumption that side effects are already tracked by a separate `sync` pass.

explanation: DCE removes computations whose results are dead and that have no side effects. In an IR with memref writes, a store to a memref is a side effect: if the memref is a function argument or otherwise reachable outside the pass's SSA horizon, removing the store is unsound. `linalg.copy` writes to %B (a caller-owned memref) — externally observable — so it must stay. `linalg.matmul` writes to %C and %C is returned — clearly live. Only the pure `arith.addf` with a dead SSA result can be safely removed.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: it treats `linalg.copy` as dead. But the copy writes to a function-argument memref, which is externally observable.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: DCE respects memory side effects and only removes the pure, dead SSA op.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: elides observable writes; violates program semantics.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: reverses the rule about SSA-value liveness and memory-store elimination.

assumptions: The IR distinguishes ops with memory side effects from pure ops (as MLIR's MemoryEffects interface does).
The caller retains a reference to the memrefs `%A`, `%B`, `%C` after the call.
nonImplications: Does not imply DCE cannot remove any memref write; if analysis proves the write is unobservable (fully-local buffer, no escape), the write can be removed.
Does not imply DCE and CSE are the same; CSE deduplicates equivalent computations.

distractorRationales.A: Ignores that the copy's write is observable.
